title: Landing page outline (activation variant) — Quickstart + Benchmarks + Troubleshooting
content:
Purpose / where this page fits
- This is an activation-focused landing page variant intended for:
  1) Retargeting (LinkedIn/Google) for non-activated signups and recently lapsed users
  2) Email CTAs (welcome/first-success/troubleshooting/next-step emails)
- Goal: reduce time-to-first-success by giving a single “production-like” path: create key → run a request (optionally streaming) → see latency/cost in Console → optional next step.
- Secondary goal: pre-empt common blockers (auth, model selection confusion, streaming disconnects) and route to the right help.

Primary success criteria (tracking)
- Primary: activation_rate_72h (as defined in sprint PRD; see taxonomy)
- Supporting: time_to_first_success (median), click-through to Console, quickstart snippet copy rate, doc scroll depth
- Guardrails: support link click rate spike, unsubscribe spike (email), SLO/perf (page load + Console perf if deep-linking)

Audience / personalization notes
- Default audience: self-serve developers evaluating Redwood API
- Secondary audience: teams comparing providers (benchmark/proof points matter)
- Personalization (lightweight, based on UTMs):
  - If utm_medium=email: emphasize “finish setup in 2 minutes” and deep-link to Console
  - If utm_medium=paid_social or paid_search: emphasize “predictable latency + cost controls” and verified benchmarks, then quickstart
  - If visitor is already logged in: swap hero CTA to “Go to Console →” and “Run a test request”

URL + routing
- Proposed path: /lp/activate-quickstart (not indexed) OR /quickstart/activate (indexed)
- Recommendation for sprint: publish /lp/activate-quickstart (noindex) for clean experimentation; evaluate SEO version post-sprint.

Page structure (outline)

1) Hero (above the fold)
- H1 (option A): “Get your first Redwood inference response in under 5 minutes.”
- H1 (option B): “Ship fast LLM inference: low latency, predictable cost, reliable serving.”
- Subhead: “Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private. Start with a single API call—then see token-level latency and cost in the Console.”
- Primary CTA (logged out): “Get API key” → /console/signup?next=/console/api-keys
- Primary CTA (logged in): “Create API key” → /console/api-keys
- Secondary CTA: “View Quickstart (curl)” anchor link to section 2
- Proof chips (tight, no over-promising):
  - “Streaming + tool calling supported”
  - “Token-level latency and cost breakdown”
  - “Dedicated + VPC options available”
- Trust line (optional): “Benchmarks and configs linked below. Results vary by model/hardware.”

2) Quickstart: one request (curl) + SDKs
- Header: “Quickstart: one request, then iterate”
- Step 0: prerequisites
  - “Create an API key” (link)
  - “Set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var”
- Step 1: curl (default)
  - Code block:
    - Export key
    - POST /v1/chat/completions (or canonical endpoint used in docs)
    - Use a stable, fast default model (align with current catalog; placeholder here): model="redwood/verified-chat"
    - Keep prompt minimal and deterministic for first success
  - Output snippet: show a sample JSON response and a request_id
- Step 2: streaming (optional but encouraged)
  - Toggle: “Prefer streaming?”
  - Short explanation: “Streaming reduces perceived latency and helps debug partial outputs.”
  - Code block for streaming in:
    - Node/TypeScript (SDK)
    - Python (SDK)
  - Callout: “If you see disconnects, jump to Streaming troubleshooting below.”
- Step 3: verify in Console
  - “Open Console → Requests” (deep-link)
  - “See latency + token usage + cost breakdown” (deep-link to usage dashboard)
- Step 4: next step (choose-one)
  - “Create a Route for production traffic” (if applicable)
  - “Enable caching/batching recommendations” (if applicable)
  - “Invite a teammate”

3) Benchmarks section (proof points + how to interpret)
- Header: “Benchmarks that map to real workloads”
- Goal: provide substantiation without being overly salesy; include methodology links.
- Content blocks:
  - “Latency (p50/p95) for streaming vs non-streaming” (mini chart or table)
  - “Cost per 1M output tokens (example configurations)” (mini table)
  - “Reliability: error rate + fallback behavior” (short description)
- Benchmarks guidelines (copy constraints):
  - Always include: model name, context length, batch settings, region, date
  - Always include a link: “Methodology” and “Reproduce this test”
  - Avoid absolute claims like “fastest”; use “competitive”, “optimized for”, “verified profiles”.
- Suggested links (placeholders; confirm with Ethan/Soojin):
  - /docs/benchmarks
  - /blog/inference-benchmark-methodology
  - /docs/optimize/batching-and-caching

4) Troubleshooting (activation blockers + fixes)
- Header: “Stuck? Fix the top onboarding issues in minutes.”
- Intro: “If you’re blocked, it’s usually one of these. If not, contact Support with request_id.”
- Accordion list (each with symptoms → likely cause → fix → link to docs):
  A) 401 Unauthorized / invalid_api_key
    - Symptoms: 401, “invalid API key”, auth header missing
    - Fix: confirm you’re using the correct header format; rotate key; check you’re hitting the right base URL
    - CTA: “Open API keys”
  B) 404 / wrong route
    - Symptoms: endpoint not found, console links 404
    - Fix: use canonical endpoint; if coming from old link, go to Console home and navigate to API
    - CTA: “Console home”
  C) 429 rate limited / quota
    - Symptoms: 429, “rate_limit_exceeded”
    - Fix: retry with backoff; request higher limits; reduce max_tokens
    - CTA: “View usage + limits”
  D) Model selection confusion
    - Symptoms: request succeeds but output quality unexpected; unsure which model to pick
    - Fix: start with recommended defaults; use eval prompt set; consider embeddings vs chat endpoint
    - CTA: “Model catalog”
  E) Streaming disconnects / partial output
    - Symptoms: stream ends early, client disconnect
    - Fix: client timeout settings; keepalive; recommended SDK streaming examples
    - CTA: “Streaming examples (Node/Python)”
  F) CORS / browser errors (if we expect browser-based experiments)
    - Symptoms: preflight failures
    - Fix: use server-side calls; configure allowed origins (if supported)
    - CTA: “Security + CORS docs”
- “Contact Support” block (last resort)
  - “Include request_id + timestamp + SDK version”
  - Link to Support portal

5) FAQ (short)
- “Can I deploy in a VPC / on-prem?” → yes, link to Redwood Private overview
- “Do you support dedicated capacity?” → yes, link to Dedicated
- “How do you handle data retention?” → link to security docs
- “What about structured output / tool calling?” → link to docs

6) Final CTA (strong, simple)
- Headline: “Run your first request now.”
- Primary CTA: “Get API key” / “Go to Console”
- Secondary CTA: “Read docs”
- Small print: “No credit card required to start (if true for current policy).”

Design/UX notes (for Tessa/Kenji)
- Keep code blocks copyable with a one-click “Copy” button (instrument copy event).
- Make “Get API key” visible after scroll (sticky header CTA).
- Avoid heavy graphics that slow LCP; prioritize fast load.
- Accessibility:
  - Ensure code blocks are selectable and have sufficient contrast.
  - Accordion keyboard navigable.

SEO notes (if/when we ship an indexed version)
- If we go indexed, separate from paid/email variant:
  - Indexed URL: /quickstart/llm-inference (example) with canonical tags
  - Keep /lp/activate-quickstart as noindex
- Title tag (draft): “LLM Inference Quickstart (Low Latency + Cost Controls) | Redwood Inference”
- Meta description (draft): “Make your first LLM inference call in minutes. Copy-paste curl + SDK examples, streaming, latency/cost visibility, and troubleshooting for common errors.”
- Target keywords (draft; validate with search volume later):
  - “LLM inference quickstart”
  - “streaming chat completions API”
  - “reduce LLM latency”
  - “LLM inference cost per token”
- On-page SEO:
  - H2s should match intent: Quickstart, Streaming, Benchmarks, Troubleshooting
  - Add FAQ schema only if we publish indexed page and content is stable

UTM + measurement plan (sprint-specific)
- This page should accept UTMs and persist them through signup → Console → first request where possible.
- Required parameters:
  - utm_source (e.g., linkedin, google, email)
  - utm_medium (paid_social, paid_search, email)
  - utm_campaign (e.g., lifecycle_activation_sprint_wk1)
  - utm_content (creative/version identifier; e.g., bench_claim_a, quickstart_a)
  - utm_term (for paid search keywords)
- Additional click IDs (do not log raw PII):
  - gclid (Google)
  - msclkid (if needed)
  - li_fat_id (LinkedIn)
- Example URLs
  - Paid social: https://redwoodinference.com/lp/activate-quickstart?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=paid_social&utm_campaign=lifecycle_activation_sprint_wk1&utm_content=bench_a
  - Email: https://redwoodinference.com/lp/activate-quickstart?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=onboarding_first_success&utm_content=cta_hero
- Instrumentation events (web)
  - lp_view (properties: utm_*, referrer, logged_in, variant_id)
  - lp_cta_click (cta_id: hero_primary, hero_secondary, sticky_cta, final_cta)
  - lp_copy_code_click (snippet_id: curl_basic, ts_stream, py_stream)
  - lp_accordion_open (topic_id)
  - lp_scroll_depth (25/50/75/90)
- Join strategy (high level)
  - Web events → user_id after signup (if consented) or anonymous_id → stitched on signup
  - Downstream: api_key_created, first_request_success, first_streaming_success, dashboard_viewed

Experiment notes / variants
- Variant A emphasis: “Fast first success” (short copy, quickstart first, benchmarks later)
- Variant B emphasis: “Proof first” (benchmarks/proof chips above fold; quickstart immediately below)
- Keep troubleshooting constant across variants to avoid confounding

Open questions / TODO
- Confirm activation definition copy: do we say “first successful request” or “first streaming success” on page?
- Confirm default model name used in snippet (must match catalog + docs PR)
- Confirm whether “no credit card required” is still accurate under credits/incentives policy
- Confirm which Console deep-links are stable (avoid 404s; see SUP-2841 risk)
- Confirm privacy copy for tracking (cookie banner behavior, consent mode)

Risks / guardrails
- If Console routes change, deep-links will break; add a short redirect-safe path or use a stable ‘/console’ entrypoint.
- Benchmark claims must be substantiated and linked; avoid absolute superlatives.
- Avoid pushing users to streaming as the only activation path if it increases error volume; keep streaming as “optional but recommended” until data proves it.

Owner checklist before launch
- [ ] UTM conventions aligned with attribution doc
- [ ] Instrumentation validated in staging; events arriving with expected properties
- [ ] QA all deep-links (logged in/out)
- [ ] Mobile layout sanity check (code blocks + copy button)
- [ ] Support contact path + request_id guidance included
- [ ] Noindex set (if running as LP experiment)
